Chastise

chas-TIZE · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To chastise to criticize or reprimand someone severely.

The editor chastised the reporter for publishing unverified claims.

Worked Example

The principal chastised the students for the prank, warning that the next offense would mean suspension.

A severe, formal reprimand with a clear warning attached is exactly what chastise describes.

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rebuke

Antonyms

praise

commend

How Strong Is It? — correct → chastise → castigate

correct vs. chastise

correct vs. chastise: To correct someone points out a mistake; to chastise them is a much sharper, more severe reprimand.

castigate vs. chastise

castigate vs. chastise: Castigate goes further than chastise, often implying a public, more formal condemnation.

Put it together

Put it together: chast ('pure', from Latin castus) + -ise together trace to the same idea as castigate -- correcting someone to make them 'pure' again.
